subject: Quantara: Budget bands + peak surge matrix
messages:
From: Sarah Park <sarah@quantara.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 15:23:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: hosted pricing inputs and usage workbook

Hi Ben —

Thanks again for the demo today. Quick post-call summary and the data we promised to share so you can put together a hosted pricing note. We had internal alignment and want to validate a committed + burst model rather than pure pay-as-you-go. High-level:

- Current plan: rolling pilot Jan–Mar 2027, then production in Q2.
- Expected steady-state consumption (post pilot): ~18.5M tokens/month.
- Typical request shape: ~80% generation (multi-turn chat + single prompt completions), ~20% embedding/rerank workloads.
- Average tokens per API request (prompt + response): ~280 tokens.
- Peak behavior: short surge windows (5–10 minutes) during product events; observed internal spike up to ~320 TPS in a 3-minute window during a load test.
- Target unit economics: Quantara is budgeting ~$30–$40 / 1M tokens; they asked whether Redwood can meet ~$30/1M on a committed slab.

Attached: quantara_usage_profile_Nov2026.xlsx (monthly slices and a 7-day peak extract).

As next steps, can you: (1) confirm whether a 25M token/month commit makes sense for initial pricing bands, (2) call out supported burst TPS and any 99th-percentile SLOs, and (3) outline any initial pilot pricing you can offer for the first 3 months?

I can loop in our Ops lead (Mike) for the SLO discussion if needed.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Park
Head of Platform
Quantara Inc.

Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: hosted pricing inputs and usage workbook

Sarah —

Appreciate the workbook and the clear asks. Quick clarifying questions before we put together a short pricing matrix and pilot offer:

1) When you say ~320 TPS spike, is that measured in requests/sec or tokens/sec? (we usually size on tokens/sec)
2) Can you confirm whether the 80% generation traffic is mostly short chat sessions (multi-turn) or large single-shot generations? That affects KV cache behavior and batching.
3) Do you need streaming responses for real-time UX during the pilot?
4) Any regulatory/storage constraints (PII retention, audit logs, SOC2) we should bake into the pricing?

We'll draft three options: pilot slab, 12-week ramp commit, and a higher-capacity commit with preferred $/1M bands for larger volume. Looping Marissa and Karthik to size the unit economics and burst windows.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Park <sarah@quantara.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mike O'Neill <mike.oneill@quantara.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 08:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: hosted pricing inputs and usage workbook

Ben — quick answers below (pulled these straight from our observability export):

1) The 320 figure is tokens/sec (we were measuring tokens entering the model) — apologies for the ambiguous phrasing.
2) The 80% generation traffic is a mix: ~65% multi-turn chat (avg session length 3.2 turns), ~15% single-shot longer completions (avg output length ~700 tokens).
3) Yes — we want streaming for the chat flows in the pilot.
4) We will need SOC2 and the ability to rotate keys via our KMS. No special data residency constraints for the pilot (US-based workloads).

Attaching a short sample of prompt patterns: quantara_prompt_samples.txt.

On the $/1M target: internal stakeholders prefer ~$30/1M if we can secure a 12-month commit after a successful pilot. If that's unrealistic, tell us what a reasonable two-tier commit looks like.

Thanks,
Sarah

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Quantara pricing draft (do not forward)

Ben —

Draft banding and pilot suggestion after looking at Sarah's workbook and the token/sec spike:

- Pilot (12 weeks): 5M committed tokens/mo at $45 / 1M, capped to a 25M total spend across pilot months. Includes streaming enabled and access to standard observability retention (30 days).
- Standard Commit A: 25M tokens/mo commit — $35 / 1M tokens; allows bursts up to 350 tokens/sec sustained for 10 minutes with automatic fallback to a compatible quantized variant if capacity constrained. 99th percentile latency SLO: 450ms for the chat workloads.
- Standard Commit B: 75M tokens/mo commit — $30 / 1M tokens; burst to 500 tokens/sec (short windows), 99th pct SLO: 350ms.

Notes: We should avoid promising unlimited bursts without a defined burst policy. Given their 320 tokens/sec observed spike, Commit A at 25M with burst to 350 would be a safe initial offer and keeps their $/1M near the $30–$40 target. For the commercial pitch, recommend a 3-month introductory discount on Commit A at $32.5 / 1M.

Attaching a quick pricing_grid_QTR-2026-334.pdf to include these bands and a pilot-friendly SOW sketch.

Marissa
Director, SalesOps

Subject: Quantara hosted pricing proposal + next steps

Sarah / Mike —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the clarifications — helpful. Based on your usage profile and the salesops banding we discussed internally, here's a concise proposal for the hosted API path and suggested next steps:

1) Pilot (recommended): 12 weeks, 5M tokens/month committed; pilot rate $45 / 1M tokens; includes streaming, SOC2 baseline, KMS integration support, and 30-day observability retention. Pilot cap: not to exceed 25M tokens across the pilot period.

2) Production commit (post-pilot): We recommend you consider Commit A as the initial production slab to balance cost and safety:
   - Commit A: 25M tokens/month at $35 / 1M tokens.
   - Burst allowance: up to 350 tokens/sec sustained for 10-minute windows; additional burst billed at a premium rate (TBD / usage).
   - 99th percentile request latency SLO (chat): 450ms.

3) Upside band: If you want to target $30 / 1M tokens, Commit B is available at 75M tokens/month (we can model a 12-month commitment).

4) Next steps: (a) confirm whether you want the 12-week pilot scope as-is, (b) we'll prepare a 1-page SOW + a short pricing addendum, and (c) legal/pricing sync — 30 minutes to finalize pilot caps and burst terms. I've attached a one-pager summary: redwood_quantara_onepager.pdf.

If you confirm the pilot scope today, we can get the SOW draft to you by EOD tomorrow.

Best regards,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
